name: Las Vegas
summary: A desert metro in the Mojave built around the casino resorts of the Strip, with a 24-hour hospitality economy, sprawling master-planned suburbs and red-rock country on its edges.

curated-2026-10.title: Las Vegas places and neighborhoods written for Prospero Dungeon
curated-2026-10.note: Well-known public places, institutions and employers from general knowledge. Businesses open and close and rents move: treat this as a snapshot for fiction. Rents are rounded estimates of typical asking ranges, not listings. Coordinates are approximate neighborhood centers.

curated-climate-2026-10.title: Approximate monthly climate for Las Vegas (Harry Reid International Airport)
curated-climate-2026-10.note: Rounded values in line with NOAA 1991-2020 normals; refresh with scripts/world when network access to NOAA is available. Summer heat is extreme (often above 110F in July) and most summer rain falls in brief monsoon storms from July to September.

neighborhoods.name: The Strip (Paradise)
neighborhoods.summary: Las Vegas Boulevard's megaresorts, casinos, arenas and high-rise condo towers in unincorporated Paradise, busy around the clock.

neighborhoods.name: Convention Center and Paradise Road
neighborhoods.summary: The blocks east of the Strip around the Las Vegas Convention Center, with older condos, apartments and off-Strip hotels.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown and Fremont Street
neighborhoods.summary: The original casino district under the Fremont Street canopy, plus Fremont East bars, city and county offices, and Symphony Park.

neighborhoods.name: Arts District (18b)
neighborhoods.summary: Former industrial blocks south of downtown turned galleries, antique shops, craft bars and restaurants, with new apartment buildings.

neighborhoods.name: Chinatown (Spring Mountain Road)
neighborhoods.summary: Miles of strip-mall restaurants along Spring Mountain Road west of the Strip, many open late for casino workers and chefs.

neighborhoods.name: Medical District
neighborhoods.summary: The hospital cluster around University Medical Center near Charleston Boulevard and US 95, with older ranch homes and apartments.

neighborhoods.name: University District
neighborhoods.summary: The area around UNLV on Maryland Parkway, with student apartments, cheap eats and midcentury houses.

neighborhoods.name: East Las Vegas
neighborhoods.summary: Working-class east valley of ranch homes and apartments, with a large Latino community and taquerias along Fremont and Charleston.

neighborhoods.name: North Las Vegas
neighborhoods.summary: A separate city of newer subdivisions, warehouses and older neighborhoods, next to Nellis Air Force Base.

neighborhoods.name: Centennial Hills
neighborhoods.summary: Northwest suburbs of stucco subdivisions and shopping centers on the road toward Mount Charleston.

neighborhoods.name: Summerlin
neighborhoods.summary: A large master-planned community on the west edge of the valley with trails, parks, a ballpark and Downtown Summerlin, beside Red Rock Canyon.

neighborhoods.name: Spring Valley
neighborhoods.summary: Central-west suburbs of apartment complexes and tract homes, where Chinatown's restaurants spill west along Spring Mountain and Rainbow.

neighborhoods.name: Southwest (Enterprise)
neighborhoods.summary: The fast-growing southwest valley of master-planned subdivisions like Mountain's Edge, plus data centers and warehouses.

neighborhoods.name: Southern Highlands
neighborhoods.summary: A master-planned community at the south end of the valley built around a private golf club, with gated enclaves.

neighborhoods.name: Green Valley (Henderson)
neighborhoods.summary: Henderson's older master-planned core of parks, schools and shopping centers, popular with families.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown Henderson
neighborhoods.summary: Henderson's original town center around Water Street, with newer subdivisions climbing toward the River Mountains.

neighborhoods.name: Lake Las Vegas
neighborhoods.summary: A resort community around a man-made lake at the eastern edge of Henderson, with Mediterranean-style condos and a village of restaurants.

neighborhoods.name: Boulder City
neighborhoods.summary: A small, quiet town built for the Hoover Dam workers, with no casinos and Lake Mead on its doorstep.

transit.name: RTC Transit buses
transit.summary: The Regional Transportation Commission's valley-wide bus network, running 24 hours on major routes.

transit.name: The Deuce
transit.summary: Double-decker RTC buses running around the clock along the Strip to downtown.

transit.name: Las Vegas Monorail
transit.summary: Elevated line behind the east side of the Strip from MGM Grand to SAHARA, with a stop at the Convention Center.

transit.name: Driving
transit.summary: How most residents get around: wide arterials, the I-15 and the 215 beltway, and plentiful parking off the Strip.

transit.name: Rideshare and taxis
transit.summary: Uber, Lyft and cabs with dedicated pickup areas at every resort and the airport.

transit.name: Walking
transit.summary: Practical on the Strip and downtown via pedestrian bridges, though distances between resorts are long and summer heat is punishing.

places.name: Fountains of Bellagio
places.summary: Free water shows set to music on the lake in front of Bellagio, every half hour or so from the afternoon.

places.name: Bellagio Conservatory & Botanical Gardens
places.summary: Free indoor garden with elaborate floral displays that change with the seasons.

places.name: "O" by Cirque du Soleil

places.name: Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign

places.name: High Roller

places.name: The LINQ Promenade

places.name: Brooklyn Bowl
places.summary: Bowling alley and concert venue on the LINQ Promenade.

places.name: Grand Canal Shoppes gondolas
places.summary: Gondola rides along indoor canals under a painted sky at The Venetian, with an outdoor canal on the Strip.

places.name: Sphere
places.summary: The LED-covered globe behind The Venetian, showing immersive films and concert residencies on a wraparound screen.

places.name: The Forum Shops at Caesars
places.summary: Luxury mall at Caesars Palace built like a Roman street, with a spiral escalator and animatronic fountain shows.

places.name: Bacchanal Buffet

places.name: Fashion Show Las Vegas
places.summary: Big indoor mall on the Strip with department stores and a runway in the center court.

places.name: Tacos El Gordo
places.summary: Tijuana-style taqueria on the north Strip with adobada shaved off the spit, open into the small hours.

places.name: Peppermill Restaurant & Fireside Lounge
places.summary: Twenty-four-hour diner and neon-lit lounge with a firepit, unchanged since the 1970s.

places.name: Hash House A Go Go at The LINQ
places.summary: Brunch spot known for enormous portions of farm-style breakfast.

places.name: Golden Steer Steakhouse

places.name: T-Mobile Arena
places.summary: Home of the Vegas Golden Knights, also used for big concerts and fights.

places.name: Allegiant Stadium
places.summary: Domed home of the Las Vegas Raiders and UNLV football, just west of I-15 from Mandalay Bay.

places.name: Shark Reef Aquarium

places.name: The STRAT SkyPod
places.summary: Observation deck atop the STRAT tower at the north end of the Strip, with thrill rides on the roof.

places.name: AREA15 and Omega Mart

places.name: Pinball Hall of Fame

places.name: Fremont Street Experience

places.name: The Mob Museum

places.name: The Neon Museum

places.name: Downtown Container Park

places.name: Atomic Liquors

places.name: Stadium Swim at Circa

places.name: The Smith Center for the Performing Arts

places.name: Discovery Children's Museum
places.summary: Three floors of hands-on exhibits in Symphony Park.

places.name: PublicUs

places.name: Esther's Kitchen
places.summary: Arts District Italian restaurant known for house-made pasta and sourdough.

places.name: Velveteen Rabbit

places.name: Arts Factory

places.name: Pho Kim Long

places.name: Raku

places.name: Freed's Bakery

places.name: Downtown Summerlin

climate.summary: Hot desert: very hot, dry summers with brief monsoon storms, mild sunny winters with cold nights, and very little rain at any time of year.

local_color.name: Locals avoid the Strip
local_color.summary: Residents mostly stay off Las Vegas Boulevard except to take visitors out, see a show or go to work, and plan routes around its traffic.

local_color.name: Locals casinos
local_color.summary: Neighborhood casinos off the Strip draw residents with cheaper food, bowling, movie theaters and player's club deals, and are where many people actually gamble.

local_color.name: Slots everywhere
local_color.summary: Slot and video poker machines stand in grocery stores, gas stations and the airport, and locals stop noticing them within a week.

local_color.name: Locals discounts
local_color.summary: Many shows, restaurants and attractions give a discount to anyone with a Nevada ID, so "Are you a local?" is a common question at the counter.

local_color.name: Saying "Nevada"
local_color.summary: Locals say it with the middle sound of "bad" (ne-VAD-a), and notice at once when someone says ne-VAH-da.

local_color.name: "But it's a dry heat"
local_color.summary: The standard half-joking reply about summer days over 40 degrees Celsius; low humidity does help, until it does not.

local_color.name: Summer heat habits
local_color.summary: In summer people hunt for shaded parking, use windshield shades, keep a towel for the steering wheel and do outdoor exercise before sunrise.

local_color.name: A 24-hour town
local_color.summary: Bars, casinos, gyms and some grocery stores never close, and so many people work swing and graveyard shifts that dinner at 3 a.m. is normal.

local_color.name: Glitter Gulch
local_color.summary: The old nickname for the neon-lit casino blocks of Fremont Street downtown, the Las Vegas of before the megaresorts.

local_color.name: Downtown shrimp cocktail
local_color.summary: The cheap shrimp cocktail in a tall glass, sold for decades by downtown casinos as a lure, is a piece of old Vegas many locals still order.

local_color.name: Buffets
local_color.summary: All-you-can-eat buffets are a Las Vegas institution, from lavish Strip spreads to cheaper ones in locals casinos.

local_color.name: Ellis Island steak special
local_color.summary: Ellis Island's cheap steak dinner special, a few blocks off the Strip, has long been one of the best-known locals bargains in town.

local_color.name: Adobada tacos
local_color.summary: Tijuana-style tacos of marinated pork carved from a spit, eaten standing up at busy taco shops late at night.

local_color.name: Chinatown on Spring Mountain
local_color.summary: Spring Mountain Road west of the Strip is a long strip of Asian restaurants where chefs and casino workers go after their shifts.

local_color.name: Vegas Golden Knights
local_color.summary: The NHL team that reached the Stanley Cup final in its first season (2018) and won the Cup in 2023, playing at T-Mobile Arena.

local_color.name: Las Vegas Raiders
local_color.summary: The NFL team moved from Oakland in 2020 and plays at Allegiant Stadium, with many visiting fans on game days.

local_color.name: Las Vegas Aces
local_color.summary: The WNBA team, champions in 2022 and 2023, playing at Michelob Ultra Arena at Mandalay Bay.

local_color.name: Las Vegas Aviators
local_color.summary: The Triple-A minor league baseball team plays in Summerlin at Las Vegas Ballpark.

local_color.name: UNLV Runnin' Rebels
local_color.summary: UNLV basketball, national champions in 1990, plays at the Thomas & Mack Center, and the city still remembers the Tarkanian years.
